methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $150M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Heirloom Carbon, a Series B climate and energy company founded by Shashank Samala and Noah McQueen, is evaluated against a comparable universe of 9 private frontier-tech operators and 1 public entity in the Climate & Energy sector.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the company's $150M+ total raised as a base proxy and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B-to-later-stage advancement, yielding $285M. Peer-median analysis anchors to three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies: KoBold Metals ($3.0B, Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B, Series C), and Amogy ($700M, Series C), producing a median of $1.0B with a range of $700M to $3.0B. These two methods triangulate to a low of $242M, median of $642M, and high of $1.1B.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $242M to $1.1B, with a median point of $642M. Key uncertainties include the wide dispersion in peer valuations—a 4.3x spread from floor to ceiling—reflecting heterogeneous capital intensity and commercialization timelines within the climate tech space. The stage-progression method relies on raised capital as a proxy rather than disclosed pre-money valuation. Resolution of these uncertainties would benefit from additional disclosure on company-specific deployment timelines and margin profiles relative to the peer set.
